title: manteen install receipt
description: What manteen wrote, where, and on whose behalf. Committed to VCS: it is a safety record, not a cache, and its value is cross-machine and CI determinism. Never edited by hand except to hand a destination back, which is done by deleting an item's entry.

$schema.description: Never emitted by manteen; preserved verbatim when present, so wiring up editor completion does not make the file churn on every run. Declared here only so `additionalProperties: false` does not reject it.

lockfileVersion.description: A reader accepts <= its own version and refuses >. Failing closed on version skew is the correct default for a file whose whole job is preventing a silent overwrite: a v2 field that CHANGES THE MEANING of a v1 field would otherwise pass unnoticed. The escape is --force.

items.description: Sorted by id. An array rather than an object map because a plain-object map returns a function for the INHERITED keys `toString` and `constructor`, so every lookup would need an Object.hasOwn guard. Cross-entry uniqueness of ids and of destinations is enforced in parseReceipt — JSON Schema cannot express it.

theme.description: The folded theme, or null when this project has no theme contribution. A theme file is folded, not owned (D5), so its destination never appears under an item.

receiptPath.description: POSIX, relative to the project root. The pattern rejects a leading slash, a Windows drive letter and any backslash; the `.`/`..` segment rule is enforced in code, because a caller may inject a no-op validator and a hand-edited receipt must never redirect a write outside the project.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex. Of the UTF-8 encoding of the STRING manteen wrote — not of the bytes on disk now. The gap between the two is the drift signal.

registry.description: The namespace this item came from; null for a bare `url:` reference, which has none. Reporters print `registry ?? sourceUrl` so two colliding url refs stay distinguishable.

sourceUrl.description: REDACTED — `${VAR}` is left literal. This file is committed; an expanded token must never reach it.

direct.description: Appeared as a root ref in some run. Sticky across refreshes, because a transitive re-reach must not demote a user's explicit install.

files.description: Sorted by destination. May be empty: a theme item whose only file was absorbed by the fold keeps its entry and shows up in `theme.sources` instead.

path.description: The SOURCE path inside the registry item, for provenance. Never a destination — nothing is written at it.

sources.description: CUMULATIVE across runs, in fold order, deduped on (itemId, path). Deliberately NOT sorted: fold order is semantic (D6), and `prefer: "base"` makes it decide which leaf survives.
